record.original_question: Consider the space of monic polynomials z maps to z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + ... + a_1 z with |a_1| >= 1, so that the origin is an unattractive fixed point, and do not assume the Julia set is connected. If at least one external ray lands at the origin, there is a rotation number for these rays under theta maps to n theta mod 1. Does this rotation number extend uniquely to a continuous map from this space of polynomials to R/Z, taking the value theta when a_1 = e^{2 pi i theta}?

evidence.quote: Consider the space of all monic polynomials z 7→ z n + an−1 z n−1 + · · · + a1 z with |a1| ≥ 1 , so that there is an unattractive fixed point at the origin.
If at least one external ray lands at the origin, then there is a well defined “rotation number” of these external rays under the map θ 7→ nθ (mod 1) .
Question 12. Does this rotation number extend uniquely to a continuous map from our space of polynomials to R/Z ? (When a1 = e2πiθ , this rotation number map must take the value θ.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be a fixed integer, and consider the space
$$\mathcal{P}_n = \{\, P(z) = z^n + a_{n-1} z^{n-1} + \cdots + a_2 z^2 + a_1 z \;:\; a_j \in \mathbb{C},\ |a_1| \geq 1\,\},$$
of monic polynomials of degree $n$ that fix the origin with multiplier $a_1$ of modulus at least $1$, so that $0$ is a non-attracting fixed point. For each such $P$, the basin of infinity carries external rays $R_\theta$ parametrized by angles $\theta \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, and the dynamics on these angles is given by $\theta \mapsto n\theta \pmod 1$. (The Julia set is not assumed to be connected, in which case external rays are defined via the Böttcher coordinate near $\infty$ and may not all extend to $\infty$ on the parameter level, but those that land at the fixed point $0$ are well defined.)

Suppose that for some $P \in \mathcal{P}_n$ at least one external ray lands at the origin. Then the set of angles of rays landing at $0$ is invariant under $\theta \mapsto n\theta \pmod 1$, and the restriction of this map to that set is conjugate to a rigid rotation by some $\rho(P) \in \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$, called the combinatorial rotation number at $0$.

Question: Does $\rho$ extend uniquely to a continuous map
$$\rho : \mathcal{P}_n \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$$
defined on the entire space $\mathcal{P}_n$, with the property that $\rho(P) = \theta$ whenever $a_1 = e^{2\pi i \theta}$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search located the foundational Goldberg–Milnor work on fixed point portraits and related papers on external rays and rotation numbers at fixed points of polynomial maps, but no source clearly resolves the question of unique continuous extension of the combinatorial rotation number to the full parameter space considered. The status appears to remain unverified in the literature accessible by search.

status_evidence.title: Fixed points of polynomial maps. Part II. Fixed point portraits
status_evidence.snippet: Goldberg–Milnor paper developing the theory of rotation numbers of external rays landing at fixed points of polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational source for combinatorial rotation numbers at polynomial fixed points; does not directly establish the continuous extension claimed in the question.

status_evidence.title: Cubic Polynomial Maps with Periodic Critical Orbit, Part I
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses landing of external rays and continuous dependence in parameter space for cubic polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: Provides continuity-of-landing results for rays in restricted families, but does not settle the general extension question.
